backend_memory_probe.method: One persistent superuser connection, prepared mget with keys 1..64, 5000 calls between samples of sum(total_bytes) in pg_backend_memory_contexts.

publication_notes: Local date 2026-09-14 UTC+3; timestamps use UTC.
Primary workload uses 64 clients, 50000 requests per non-cold sample, and max_connections=300.
Fixed-build sweep: 4/64/256 connections at max_connections=300. Legacy sweeps were sequential: 1/4/16/32, then 64 at max_connections=100; 128/256 after recreating the demo with max_connections=300.
pgbench stdout temporary SQL file paths are replaced with <temporary directory>/read.sql; numerical measurements are unchanged.
Client work and CPU timing boundaries differ between Node.js and pgbench; see docs/BENCHMARKS.md.
Two full workload attempts on 2.0.1 failed during SQL warm-up. The published full run uses the SPI-plan lifetime fix; the harness additionally preserves partial output on failure.
